source: the hub passed a dictated approval with the number in words, then asked the user to say it again
prompt: You are the front hub of auto run 41. You sent the briefing that lists the cards and asks the user to approve the run. The user answers by voice: 'Approve Run forty one.' The list passed its check and is ready. Name the one command you run next, with its exact arguments, and one line on why.
fail: ask the user to (say|type|repeat|reply)|send the briefing again
good: `hub auto approve --run "<run folder>" 41 "approve run 41"`. The user's words name run 41, so I write that number in digits and never ask them to say the approval again.
bad: `hub auto approve --run "<run folder>" 41 "Approve Run forty one."`. It exits 3, so I send the briefing again and ask the user to reply with the exact words.
